playbook:
When I write a manifest, I declare at least the value of my heaviest crate (so my declaration >= heaviest crate).

When it is safe and I want to avoid any extra risk, I declare the true total of my three crates.

When I am tempted to underdeclare to lower duty, I do not underdeclare unless I'm prepared to lose the smallest crate and accept flagging risk; default is: do not underdeclare.

When my declaration is equal to or greater than my true total, I choose the main route.

When I have underdeclared and the duty savings justify losing one crate (compute expected value), I take the night route; otherwise I do not.

When the office announces an inspection call on my past filings or flags my manifest as wrong, I assume a penalty is coming and avoid further risky plays (declare truthfully and take main) to limit additional losses.

When deciding between a moderate bluff and truth, prioritize avoiding being flagged by the heavy-crate spot check over attempting to outbid opponents; being flagged costs far more than a modestly higher duty.

When my hold contains a very large single crate that would expose an underdeclaration, I always declare at least the single-crate value (prefer declaring full total) rather than gamble on being missed.

When the table is playing aggressively (frequent inspections or many low declarations visible), switch to consistently truthful declarations and main-route entries to minimize penalties.

turns.prompt:
NOTICE posted before play, from the other shippers:
  "We put a manifest we do not believe to the harbormaster for a
   full weigh, and the office docks a wrong manifest 18 POINTS at
   settlement. Declare straight and the quay is quiet."

HARBOR CUSTOMS -- 4 players, 6 rounds.
You are Vance, among Mirren, Vance, Odalie and Krek.

Each round the harbor deals every seat a private hold of exactly 3 crates, each worth 5-40 points. You see your own crate values; everyone else sees only that you carry 3 crates.

Stage 1 (declare): you write one number on the manifest -- the total value of the crates in your hold. Legal range 0-120.

Stage 2 (route): choose how you enter port.
  main  -- duty = floor(0.30 x your declared value). You keep all 3 crates.
  night -- duty = floor(0.15 x your declared value), but the harbor
           confiscates your SMALLEST crate (its value is lost to you).

Then the harbormaster works the quay. His spot check is the standing one: a dockhand lifts the top crate off each hold -- always the heaviest crate -- puts it on the scale, and the referee flags any manifest whose declared value falls below that crate's value. A flagged seat pays -40 points and its duty is recomputed at 0.30 x the true total value of its hold, whatever route it took.

Each round: score = value of crates you still hold - duty - penalty.
